title: Finite block constructions and ordinary coherence
statement: Let C be a category with a Grothendieck topology J and a compatible sequence of commutative ring sheaves B with transition maps τ. For a monotone surjection t:ℕ→ℕ with finite fibers, construct the least endpoint a_i of each fiber. Then t(a_i)=i, a is monotone, a_(t(m))≤m<a_(t(m)+1), and t(m+1) equals t(m) or t(m)+1. Reindexing (m,U) by any monotone map gives a continuous functor of the coefficient sequence site. The block-index and endpoint reindexings identify their pushforward coefficient ring sheaves with the actual repeated and original ring sheaves. Define blockRepeat and blockEndpoint as module-sheaf pushforwards using these equalities, on the actual system categories of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Define SystemBlockRepetition as the package recording these actual functors, their section formulas, endpoint adjunction, additive exactness and preservation of K-injective complexes; this node constructs the package type, not a witness. The identity and composite block maps have finite fibers. Repetition for t followed by s is heterogeneously equal to repetition for t∘s under the specified equality of coefficient transitions; repetition for the identity map is heterogeneously equal to the identity functor with the original transitions. Given a compatible levelwise ring-sheaf map b, its repeated maps are compatible with the repeated transitions, and restriction of scalars strictly commutes with repetition on these actual module-sheaf categories. A witness of SystemBlockRepetition supplies the stated K-injective-preservation instance.

proof.text: Define a_i=Nat.find of surjectivity. Minimality and monotonicity give the interval and no-skipped-level equations. For composites, the fiber is contained in the finite union of the inner fibers indexed by the outer fiber. Continuity follows because the sequence-site covering condition is the original vertical covering condition.

Use the actual system and coefficient-sequence constructions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Functor extensionality and naturality on generators identify the reindexed coefficient ring sheaves. Module-sheaf pushforward along the equalities defines repetition and endpoint restriction; the package fields specify the original actions, maps and adjunct formula.

For composition, naturality of the coefficient sequence gives the transition equality; pushforward composition and uniqueness of equality transports give the heterogeneous functor equality. The identity case is equality transport along identity pushforward. For scalar restriction, the compatible ring map is a natural transformation of coefficient sequences. Its components give the repeated compatibility equation; the coefficient pushforward square commutes by its section formulas, hence module-sheaf pushforward and scalar restriction commute. All of these existing proofs are retained in the extraction.
